transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I feel worn out all the time no matter how much I rest, like I don’t have any energy left to get through work or take care of things at home. It just feels like I'm running on empty every single day, and I don't know what to do about it anymore.
Do you also experience any kind of pain, such as headaches or muscle aches, alongside this feeling of fatigue?
I haven't really experienced physical pain like headaches or muscle aches. I do feel generally tense all the time, though, and just completely physically exhausted.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling sad, hopeless, or depressed, alongside this persistent fatigue?
I don't really feel sad or hopeless, but I do feel extremely exhausted and tense. I'm just constantly overwhelmed by worry about our financial situation and how we're going to make ends meet.
Can you tell me more about these worries, are they excessive and interfering with your daily life, or are they more related to real-life problems that you're facing?

They started with real struggles like my hours being cut, but now they've snowballed into constant worst-case scenarios, like us getting evicted or my mom getting sick, even when nothing is immediately happening. It is definitely interfering with my life because I've made mistakes at the register at work, and I'm too drained to help with chores, go to church, or spend time with my wife.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your worries, or are you able to push through them despite feeling anxious?

Yes, I definitely find myself avoiding things because I'm just too drained and on edge from all the worrying. I've been skipping church events, putting off chores, and spending less time with my wife. I've also completely pulled back from hobbies I used to love, like gardening, fishing, and volunteering.
Can you tell me if there are any times or situations when you feel a significant reduction in your worries and tension, or if they are pretty constant throughout the day?

The worries and tension are pretty much constant and don't really let up. Even during quiet moments or when I try to do things I used to enjoy, like gardening or fishing, I still feel tense and unable to relax, like I'm always waiting for the next thing to go wrong.

Have you experienced significant anxiety or fear in situations where most people would not, such as in public places or when separated from loved ones, or is your anxiety more focused on specific worries like your financial situation?

No, I don't really worry about being in public or away from my family. My anxiety is highly focused on everyday things like our finances, paying rent, my work hours, or my mother's health. Once those thoughts start, they quickly snowball uncontrollably into worst-case scenarios that I just can't shut off.

You mentioned you've pulled back from hobbies you used to love, but can you tell me if you still find any pleasure or enjoyment in the activities you do participate in, or has that been affected as well?

Yes, my ability to enjoy things has been heavily affected, and that sense of ease I used to get from gardening, fishing, or volunteering is just completely gone. Even when I try to spend time with my wife or do daily activities, I feel too physically drained, tense, and mentally distracted by my worries to find any real pleasure or relaxation. I just can't seem to shake the stress long enough to enjoy anything anymore.
Can you think of any activities or things that you used to enjoy that still bring you some pleasure or excitement, no matter how small it may seem?

I used to find so much peace and enjoyment in gardening, fishing, and volunteering at my church, but now I am just too exhausted and worried to do them. Even when I try to think about those hobbies, the constant worry and fatigue just drain any excitement or pleasure I used to get from them. It feels like there is nothing left in me to enjoy anymore.

You've mentioned that you've lost pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, but can you tell me if there are any times, even briefly, when you feel a sense of pleasure or enjoyment, or if it's completely absent?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't thought about it much because I'm usually just too exhausted and overwhelmed by everything to even notice.
Can you think of any small things, like a favorite meal, a beautiful sunset, or a funny joke, that still bring you a little bit of happiness or pleasure, even if it's just for a moment?

It has just been incredibly hard to find joy or peace in anything lately, even the small things. I used to find real comfort and happiness in simple things like gardening, fishing, or volunteering at my church. But now, because I'm constantly exhausted and my mind is always racing with worry, those things just don't bring me that same sense of ease or pleasure anymore.
Do you ever feel so down or hopeless that you've thought life wasn't worth living, or have you had any thoughts of self-harm?

No, I have never had any thoughts of self-harm or felt that life isn't worth living. I am just incredibly exhausted and overwhelmed by all the constant worry, but I've never thought about anything like that.

You've mentioned losing pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, but can you tell me if there are any times when you feel even a slight sense of pleasure or enjoyment, or is it completely absent from your life right now?
It's really hard to say if it's completely gone. Most of the time, I am just too tired and anxious to even notice or think about whether I'm experiencing any enjoyment.

Can you describe how your worries and tension affect your daily functioning, such as your ability to concentrate, make decisions, or complete tasks, and do you feel like you're able to control your worries or do they feel uncontrollable?

My worries feel completely uncontrollable, easily snowballing from a simple thought about rent into worst-case scenarios that I just can't shut off. This makes it incredibly hard to concentrate at work, where I've zoned out and made mistakes at the register that my manager has had to talk to me about twice. By the time I get home, I'm so drained that I end up putting off chores, skipping church events, and having no energy left for my wife.
Can you think of any activities or things that you still look forward to or feel excited about, even if it's just a little bit?

It is really hard to look forward to or feel excited about anything right now because I just feel so completely drained. I used to really enjoy gardening, fishing, and volunteering at church events, but lately, I’ve lost that sense of ease and don't have the energy to participate in or look forward to them anymore.
Can you tell me if your lack of energy and exhaustion are present even when you're not actively worrying about something, or do they seem to be directly tied to your episodes of worry and anxiety?

The exhaustion is pretty much constant and is there even when I'm not actively focusing on a specific worry. I wake up feeling completely drained before the day even starts, and because that tension is always running in the background, the tiredness never really lets up.
Can you tell me if you've experienced any significant weight changes, either gain or loss, or changes in your appetite over the past few months?
I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my weight or appetite recently. My eating habits have stayed pretty much the same despite all the stress.
Can you describe how your worries and anxiety affect your sleep patterns, such as difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or experiencing restless sleep?

My sleep is highly disrupted; most nights I just lie awake staring at the ceiling for an hour or two with my mind racing about bills and work shifts. Even when I finally fall asleep, I keep waking up around three or four in the morning and can't settle back down because I immediately start worrying about the next day.

Can you tell me if you have ever felt a period of at least two weeks where you didn't worry as much and felt more energetic and able to enjoy activities, or has this feeling of constant worry and exhaustion been persistent without any significant breaks?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. Ever since my hours were cut about a year and three months ago, this has been a constant, daily struggle. I haven't had even a two-week period where I felt energetic or free from worry; it just hasn't let up.

Can you tell me if you have ever felt a period where you were completely free from worry and able to enjoy activities without any anxiety, even if it was just for a short time, or has this feeling of worry been a constant presence in your life?

No, I haven't had any periods where I felt completely free from it; it has been a constant, unrelenting presence ever since my hours were cut about a year and three months ago. This constant tension has completely taken away the ease and enjoyment I used to find in my hobbies, like gardening, fishing, and volunteering.
Can you describe if your worries and anxiety are more about specific, everyday concerns like finances and work, or if they are more generalized and free-floating, not focused on any particular issue?

My worries are mostly focused on everyday things like our finances, my work hours, the car, and my mother's health. But it also feels very generalized because even when nothing is actively wrong, I still feel a constant, tense feeling like I'm just waiting for something bad to happen and can't shut my mind off.

Can you tell me if you have ever felt a period of persistent sadness or loss of interest in activities that lasted for at least two weeks, or has your main issue been the constant worry and anxiety you've described?

While I have stopped doing the things I used to enjoy, like gardening, fishing, and volunteering, because I feel completely exhausted and drained, I wouldn't say I feel a deep, persistent sadness. The core, constant issue for me is definitely this overwhelming worry and anxiety about money and keeping up with my responsibilities.

Can you think of any activities or things that you used to enjoy, but now no longer find pleasure in, and if so, have you tried to participate in them recently to see if you still derive any enjoyment from them?

I used to find a lot of peace and enjoyment in gardening, fishing, and volunteering at my church. I haven't really tried to do them lately because I feel too exhausted and drained, and I've been skipping church events entirely. My mind is just too occupied with worry, and I simply lack the energy to participate.

Can you tell me if you've ever had a period where you felt so anxious or worried that you had physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling, or if your anxiety has always been more about persistent worry and tension without these physical symptoms?

No, I've never really had those sudden physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling. Instead, my anxiety is a constant, persistent worry where I just feel physically tense all the time, like I'm waiting for something bad to happen. It just leaves me feeling completely worn out and drained of energy every single day.

Can you tell me if you have ever felt a period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently sad or empty, or if your main experience has been the worry and anxiety you've described, without a significant period of feeling sad or depressed?

No, I haven't ever had a period of persistent sadness or emptiness. My main struggle has definitely been the constant worry and feeling completely worn out. While I am overwhelmed by the stress, it is the non-stop worrying about our bills, my shifts, and my family's security that drives how I feel, rather than feeling depressed.

Can you clarify if your lack of interest in activities and feelings of exhaustion are primarily driven by your worries and anxiety, or if you feel like you would still lack interest and energy even if your worries were resolved?

Yes, my exhaustion and lack of interest are definitely driven by the constant worrying. The mental strain of stressing about bills all day, combined with losing sleep at night because of my racing mind, is what completely drains my energy. If these worries were resolved, I really believe I would get my energy back and return to enjoying gardening, fishing, and volunteering again.

If you were to imagine that all your financial worries and stressors were suddenly resolved, do you think you would still struggle to find pleasure or interest in the activities you used to enjoy, or would you expect to regain your enthusiasm for them?

I deeply miss gardening, fishing, and volunteering at my church, and while I would hope to regain my enthusiasm if the money issues went away, I think I'd still struggle at first. My mind has become so wired to constantly worry and wait for the next disaster that I feel like I wouldn't be able to fully relax or find that old sense of ease right away.
Can you think of any situations or times when you felt anxious or worried without any apparent reason or trigger, or have your worries always been tied to specific concerns like finances or work?

My worries usually start with concrete things like money, my work schedule, or my mom's health, but I also carry this constant baseline tension. Even when nothing bad is actually happening in the moment, I still feel anxious and on edge. It just feels like I am constantly waiting for the next thing to go wrong.

If your worries about finances, work, and other responsibilities were to suddenly disappear, do you think you would still feel a lack of pleasure or interest in activities, or would that improve significantly?

I really believe my interest and pleasure would improve significantly if those worries disappeared. Right now, I only lack enjoyment in gardening, fishing, and volunteering because I am constantly exhausted and my mind is always consumed by financial stress. It's not a permanent loss of interest; I just don't have the mental or physical energy for them right now.
Can you tell me if you've ever had a period where you felt so down or depressed that you lost interest in almost all activities, or has your main struggle always been with worry and anxiety?

My main struggle has always been the constant worry and anxiety, rather than feeling deeply depressed. I only stopped doing things like gardening and fishing because the non-stop worrying about our finances and my shifts leaves me completely exhausted and mentally drained. It's that constant, racing worry that keeps me from having any energy to enjoy things.
